points.t: **Flesh-coloured coalescing genital papules** after sexual contact, or a **recurrent painful groin nodule** with scarring.
Low-risk **HPV 6 / 11** in basal keratinocytes (warts); **follicular occlusion and autoinflammation** in HS.
Warts: expectant care, **podophyllotoxin / imiquimod / cryotherapy** via sexual-health pathways + HPV vaccine catch-up. Groin HS: smoking / weight, antiseptic wash, topical clindamycin ± doxycycline.
Don’t call every papule a wart (**PPP / Fordyce are normal**). Chronic white itchy scarring → **lichen sclerosus**. **Children with anogenital warts** → safeguarding-aware specialist.

cause.lead: Two common perineal problems, plus look-alikes.
points: **Warts**: sexually acquired HPV 6 / 11 through microabrasions; incubation weeks–months.
**HS**: follicular occlusion → tunnels and scarring in apocrine folds; smoking and obesity drive it; **not contagious**.
**Molluscum**: poxvirus; adult genital disease may be STI-context.
**PPP and Fordyce**: normal variants (angiofibromas; ectopic sebaceous glands).

features.lead: Warts coalesce; HS tunnels; variants line up.
points: **Warts**: flesh, pink, grey or brown verrucous papules → cauliflower plaques (vulva, penis, scrotum, perianal); often asymptomatic, itch, bleeding, distress.
**Groin HS**: recurrent painful nodules / abscesses, **double-ended comedones**, sinus tracts, rope-like scars.
Hurley I: abscesses without tracts; II: separated tracts / scarring; III: diffuse interconnected tracts.

visuals.caption: Hurley staging of hidradenitis: I nodules / abscesses without tunnels; II separate tunnels with scarring; III interconnected tunnels across the area.
visuals.alt: Three skin cross-sections showing Hurley I–III

points: Usually clinical; **biopsy** if atypical, ulcerated or resistant.
Offer STI screen and partner discussion; HPV typing not needed.
Clinical (lesions + sites + chronicity); swabs often grow colonisers.
Warts: specialist paediatric / SHS + safeguarding.

cards.name: Furuncle vs HS
cards.clue: Single acute boil without tracts or multi-site history.

manage.lead: NICE CKS themes; sexual-health services for clinic treatments.

points: ~30% regress in months: **no treatment** is valid.
Recurrence is common (latent HPV).
**HPV vaccine catch-up** if eligible (routine Year 8; catch-up to 25th birthday; GBMSM / immunosuppressed schedules differ).
**Podophyllotoxin** or **imiquimod** per SmPC; teach exact application; **avoid podophyllotoxin in pregnancy**.
Cryotherapy, TCA (often preferred in pregnancy), excision / electrosurgery via SHS.
Smoking cessation, weight, loose clothing, absorbent dressings.
Antiseptic wash (e.g. chlorhexidine) + **topical clindamycin**.
Oral doxycycline (or tetracycline) as a **prolonged** anti-inflammatory course.
Hurley II–III / refractory HS → dermatology.

limits.t: PPP / Fordyce: reassure. Molluscum: often expectant. Candida: topical azole ± brief hydrocortisone.
Not ‘thrush forever’: potent steroid pathway and referral.

items.t: Anogenital warts in a child: safeguarding-aware specialist referral.
Hurley II–III HS, non-healing ulcer in long-standing sinuses (SCC risk), LS with architectural change.

pearls.t: Condoms reduce but don’t abolish HPV transmission.
Incision and drainage alone almost always fails in HS.
Sexual-health interface: STI screen, partners, vaccine catch-up.
Verify the current Green Book HPV schedule and BNF / SmPC before advising.

quiz.q: Uniform rows of tiny papules on the corona?
Wart treatment to avoid in pregnancy?
Does HPV vaccine clear existing warts?
quiz.a: No; may protect against other types.

quiz.q: Why does I&D alone fail in HS?
quiz.a: It treats the abscess, not the tunnels / disease.
